transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess what finally got me to come in is I just don’t want to do the things that usually keep me going anymore. I’m a carpenter, and normally I can walk into my shop and just the smell of the wood — cedar, oak, sawdust in the air — it kind of settles me, you know? But lately even stepping in there feels like nothing. Like I’m looking at someone else’s life.

And it’s not just work. I used to look forward to salsa nights, church gatherings, cooking for the neighbors… little things that made me feel connected and useful. Now I either don’t go, or I think about going and just can’t make myself care. It’s strange, because those things have always been part of who I am, and lately it feels like that part of me has gone quiet. That’s what brings me in.
How long have you been feeling this way — like you don’t enjoy the things you used to and that part of you has gone quiet?

It’s been… about six months, I’d say. Maybe a little more if I’m being honest with myself, because at first I kept telling myself it was just a rough patch, or I was tired, or work had been wearing on me. You know, everybody has a bad week here and there.

But this has dragged on long enough that it doesn’t feel like that anymore. It’s not like one bad week where I could sleep it off or get through a job and feel better. It’s been month after month of that same flatness, like the color’s been turned down on everything. Six months is a long time to keep waiting for yourself to snap back.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah… yes, I do. It’s not just a sad moment here and there. Most mornings I wake up and before I’ve even really opened my eyes, there’s this heavy, empty feeling sitting right in my chest. Like the whole house has lost its color somehow — everything looks the same, but it feels drained.

And I try to get up and act normal, especially around my wife. I don’t want to scare her or make her feel like she has to carry me, so I’ll go through the motions, make coffee, stand there at the counter, but inside I’m just… holding myself together. Some mornings I feel like if she asks me the wrong gentle question, I might just break down right there in front of her. So I swallow it down and try to keep my face steady.

It’s most of the day, too. It might lift a little around the edges sometimes, but that heaviness is pretty much there nearly every day.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or that you can't sit still and feel restless?

Yeah… people have noticed that at work. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I used to be pretty steady and efficient in the shop. But lately there are times I feel like I’m moving through mud. I’ll go to pick up a board or measure something, and it takes me forever, like my boots are full of wet cement and my body just won’t get the message.

And then other times it’s the opposite, but not in a productive way. I’ll pace around the shop, rubbing my hands, walking from one bench to another, looking at tools or pieces of wood like I’m about to do something, but I don’t actually get anything done. The guys can see it. I can tell they’re trying not to make a big deal of it, but they’ve noticed.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or like you don’t have any energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing much?

Yes. Very much so. It’s one of the things that scares me a little, because it doesn’t feel like normal tired. I’ve been tired plenty of times in my life — I’m a carpenter, I know what it feels like to work a long day, frame something overhead, haul lumber, come home sore and beat up. That kind of tired makes sense.

This is different. I can have a full night in bed, or at least spend the whole night there, and when I get up my body still feels worn out, like I’ve already put in a full day framing a roof in the heat. Like I’m starting the morning from empty.

Even small things feel too big sometimes. Loading tools into the truck, which I’ve done a thousand times without thinking, can feel like this whole mountain of a task. I’ll stand there looking at the toolboxes, knowing exactly what needs to go where, and it feels like my arms don’t want to lift them. Or like just the thought of doing it takes the wind out of me before I’ve even started.

And it’s not like I have to be doing much for it to hit me. I can sit down for a while, thinking maybe I’ll catch my breath, and I don’t really come back with any more energy. I just sit there feeling heavy and used up. It makes me feel useless, honestly, because these are basic things I should be able to do.
Have you been feeling like you're not worth much or that you're letting people down, even when there's no real reason for it?

Yeah… I do. More than I want to admit.

A lot of it is around my wife. I keep going back over things in my head, over and over, like I’m reviewing a bad cut I made on a job and trying to find the exact moment I messed it up. Every appointment, every conversation, every time something changed with her health — I replay it and think, why didn’t I notice more? Why didn’t I ask a better question? Why didn’t I push harder, or protect her somehow?

And I know, logically, maybe there isn’t some one thing I could’ve done. People tell me that. But it doesn’t really land. In my head it turns into, a better husband would have caught it sooner. A better husband would’ve been more on top of it, would’ve seen the signs, would’ve known what to do instead of just… standing there trying to understand after the fact.

It makes me feel like I failed at the one job that matters most. Like I can build things for other people, fix things, measure twice and make sure it’s right — but when it came to her, I didn’t do enough. And I carry that around all day. Even when nobody is blaming me, I’m blaming myself.
Have you had any thoughts about ending your life or that life isn’t worth living anymore?

Yeah… I have. I don’t like saying that out loud.

It’s not like I’m sitting there with some clear plan in my head, but I do get these thoughts where I think… maybe it would just be easier if I didn’t wake up. Like if I could go to sleep and just not have to face another day feeling this way. And then I feel ashamed even thinking that, because I know how that sounds.

Sometimes it goes further in my head, not in a way I’m proud of. I catch myself thinking maybe my family would be better off without me dragging everybody down, without them having to worry about me or see me like this. And then that scares me, because part of me knows I wouldn’t want to put them through that, but the thought still shows up anyway.

I’ve tried to push it away and tell myself it’s just a bad thought, but… yeah. Life has felt not worth it at times. More than I want to admit.
